question.problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨\sqrt[3]{y}+x,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}⟩
$$

through the boundary of the rectangle with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(2,1),$ and $(0,1).$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14224656/assets/ea6c25e40b6683d9ff4a4884dbbda708fd79dbd79d0b50730f9ad6e165d2eb58.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=\sqrt[3]{y}+x$ and $Q(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-6{x}^{2}y.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the rectangular region $D$ as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1-6{x}^{2}y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(1-6{x}^{2}y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x-2{x}^{3}y)\,{|}_{0}^{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(2-2(2)^{3}y)-0]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2-16y)\,dy \\  & =[2y-8{y}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(2(1)-8(1)^{2})-0 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
